question: A team wants to decide whether a lighter tier is good enough for its weekly summary work. What is the most reliable way to make that call?
options: A) Run real examples of their own summaries on both tiers and judge them against an agreed standard.
B) Read published comparisons of the tiers and adopt whichever one they describe as sufficient.
C) Adopt the lighter tier and revisit that decision if the team's allowance stops running out so early.
D) Ask Claude to compare its own output on both tiers and report which version is the stronger.
correct_answers: A) Run real examples of their own summaries on both tiers and judge them against an agreed standard.
explanations: Correct. Adequacy is specific to the task and the bar, so only their own work compared against a stated standard answers the question.
Incorrect. General descriptions cannot tell the team whether a lighter tier meets their particular standard on their own material.
Incorrect. Allowance consumption measures cost, not whether the summaries still meet the required standard.
Incorrect. A self-assessment is not independent evidence, and it has not been told what this team's summary must achieve.
